# Goban Studio v18.1.0

v18.1 makes the first hour calmer and the review clearer, and closes a few
gaps in the desktop shell. It reads everything v9–v18 saved; nothing has
to be converted.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.msi` (installer, recommended) | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64), portable | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. v18.1 needs macOS 13 or
later. Your games, progress and settings are kept outside the app — in
`~/Library/Application Support/dev.hxddh.gobanstudio` on macOS and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.hxddh.gobanstudio\Data` on Windows — so replacing the
app keeps them.

## Starting out

- **No language screen.** The app opens in your system's language; four
  quiet language names in the corner change it.
- **Levels in words, not a slider.** Someone who plays picks one of five
  descriptions (now and then, regularly, a club player, around 1 dan,
  strong dan), and that pick starts the game. Your level then adjusts
  itself from your games. Every answer reaches a board in two clicks.
- **Today is one row lighter.** Today's practice and "A problem for
  today" are one row now; when the next item is a problem, the row shows
  its board and opens it in one click.

## Playing and reviewing

- **Teaching mode interrupts less.** It stops only for a move that
  changes the game — a blunder, or a mistake that turns a won game into a
  lost one. Smaller slips are still marked in the move list and wait for
  the review.
- **See the better line.** Opening a key moment in the review puts the
  recommended line on the board at once: its first five moves as numbered
  see-through stones.
- **The human-style opponent, offered where it matters.** After a game
  against the computer, and in New game with a kyu opponent, one quiet
  line offers the 99 MB human-style model, with Download and a close
  button that hides it for good.

## Looks and words

- **The dark theme.** The light board sits in a narrow frame of darker
  wood and warm shade instead of directly on black; the move list's black
  stones are black with a fine light edge.
- **Classic games** in the Library show a small window around one of
  their key moves, that move marked, instead of a noisy whole board.
- **Chinese.** More natural Go wording throughout (复盘本局, 推荐变化,
  实战进行), and 计算胜负 where 数目 was wrong under Chinese rules.

## Under the hood

- Importing many SGF files at once: every file picked (up to 256 at a
  time) can be read; before, the first ones of a large selection were
  refused.
- Updates: the macOS package's entries are checked (names, count and
  size) before it is unpacked, as on Windows.
- Downloads through a proxy: a redirect to another host follows
  `NO_PROXY` and the proxy settings for that host.
- Two rare crashes fixed: a damaged write request from the page, and a
  path read after its buffer was gone when looking for the engine.

## Known limits

- **Platform code has not been tried by hand.** The Metal and AVX2
  engines and their fallback, the speed they reach, a save surviving a
  power cut, the macOS title bar following the app's appearance, and the
  Windows installer pass their tests and the packaged self-test on CI,
  but nobody has run them on a real Mac or PC. Settings → Engines →
  Measure speed is there to check the first two; please report what it
  shows.
- **Not checked by people.** The board's colours and the new onboarding levels were
  chosen without testing them on players; the stone sounds and animations, the lessons, the KataGo
  notes on the classics, the move verdicts and the strings in Chinese,
  Korean and Japanese have not been reviewed by a strong player or native
  speakers.
- **Lessons KataGo disagrees with.** A few lessons on small 9×9 boards
  teach the local shape while KataGo prefers a big point elsewhere, and
  the 3-3 joseki teaches the standard connection where KataGo prefers a
  cut (`docs/lesson-audit.md`); they are left as taught.
- **The builds are not code-signed**, the installer included. macOS and
  Windows warn on first launch; the README in each download says what to
  do.
- **No Traditional Chinese interface.** The problem bank tops out at
  about 5 kyu.
